subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — revenue share and reseller economics
messages:
From: Alex Reynolds <alex@acme.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace path for enterprise purchase

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. Procurement at Acme is pushing us to buy via the AWS Marketplace (private offer) so we can leverage existing payment and PO processes. We expect an initial commitment of $1.2M USD year 1 (annual contract), with potential expansion in year 2.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirmation that Redwood can do an AWS private offer that includes a reseller on the order (ResellCo).
- Clarity on the reseller revenue share / commission that will appear on the marketplace invoice.
- Any AWS marketplace fees we should expect and whether Redwood will cover or pass through.

Please loop in the relevant finance / channel folks so we can move quickly — procurement wants terms in the next 7 business days. I've attached Acme_RFP_procurement.pdf for their standard contract language.

Best,
Alex Reynolds
Procurement, Acme Corporation
Attachment: Acme_RFP_procurement.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com, taylor@resellco.com, alex@acme.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Marketplace path for enterprise purchase

Team — forwarding Acme's procurement request. TL;DR: $1.2M ARR ask, want purchase via AWS private offer and include ResellCo as reseller on the invoicing path.

Initial thoughts / items we need to decide:
- Reseller revshare percentage to appear on the Marketplace invoice (ResellCo is asking for 12–18% typical).
- Whether Redwood absorbs AWS marketplace surcharge or passes it through (AWS fee ~12-20% depending on listing type).
- Discounting profile for a 1yr commitment vs. our list price to protect gross margin.

I've attached a draft pricing workbook with margin waterfall to play with numbers (pricing-workbook-v3.xlsx). Please review and call out acceptable reseller splits and minimum gross margin target (we usually aim for 30% after infra/AWS fees).

Karthik: can you advise channel strategy here (commission vs. reseller share)?
Marissa: need quick sanity check on margin math if we give ResellCo 15% on ARR.
Monica: legal will need to review reseller clause on the Marketplace order flow — flagging for review.

Thanks — Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: pricing-workbook-v3.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 08:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace path for enterprise purchase

Hi Jasmine / Karthik,

Thanks for the heads up. Confirming a Private Offer is the right path for Acme. A few notes:
- Marketplace seller fee depends on the program; for a standard Private Offer with a reseller, expect a 12% listing fee plus any reseller cut that you define on the deal.
- AWS supports reseller annotations on the invoice for traceability; the partner (ResellCo) will need to be registered and linked to your seller account.
- We recommend structuring as 1yr upfront committed usage to simplify billing and apply marketplace incentives.

Docs: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/tour/ (link)

Happy to run the PO flow with you — if you share the proposed numbers we can pre-validate in our sandbox and confirm the invoice breakout.

Regards,
Rohit Sen
AWS Marketplace Sales
aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Marketplace path for enterprise purchase

On Wed, Jan 13, 2027 at 08:41 AM AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com> wrote:
> Hi Jasmine / Karthik,
> 
> Thanks for the heads up. Confirming a Private Offer is the right path...

Team — quick channel guidance: two common ways to compensate ResellCo here:
1) Reseller revenue share on invoice (appears on AWS invoice). Simpler for partner; transparent but reduces our list net. Typical range 10–18%.
2) One-off referral/commission outside of Marketplace (Redwood pays ResellCo via partner program), preserves invoice net but requires Redwood to handle payments and tracking.

Given Acme's insistence on marketplace billing and the reseller wanting visibility, option (1) is preferred operationally. If we pick option (1), I suggest a 12% reseller revshare to keep our post-AWS-fee gross margin near 28–32% for this deal.

Marissa — can you confirm with the workbook what a 12% reseller cut + 12% AWS fee does to gross margin at the proposed ARR and our cost profile? If that doesn't work, let's iterate discounts rather than a higher reseller share.

Karthik
Head of Channels, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 15:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Marketplace path for enterprise purchase — margin scenarios

On Thu, Jan 14, 2027 at 11:05 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — quick channel guidance...

Attached a short excerpt from the pricing workbook with three scenarios: 10%, 12%, 15% reseller revshare. Key lines:
- With 12% reseller + 12% AWS fee + our infra cost assumptions, net to Redwood sits at ~30.5% gross margin at $1.2M ARR (close to target).
- At 15% reseller, margin drops to ~27% which is below our normal floor for strategic deals unless we increase list price or apply a smaller customer discount.
- Suggest we hold reseller at 12% and offer Acme a 10–15% committed-volume discount structure (tiered) to hit their price expectations while protecting margin.

I've attached redwood-pricing-model.csv with the math and the workbook saved as pricing-workbook-v3.xlsx in the thread. If you want, I can produce a short memo for ACE approval.

Marissa Cole
Director, Finance — GTM, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-pricing-model.csv, pricing-workbook-v3.xlsx (attachment stubs)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: alex@acme.com, taylor@resellco.com
Cc: aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 Jan 2027 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed marketplace economics and next steps

Alex / Taylor — thanks for the patience while we ran this internally.

Proposed terms (summary):
- Offer type: AWS Marketplace Private Offer, 1yr upfront commitment.
- Contract value: $1.2M ARR (as discussed).
- Reseller revshare: 12% of ARR to ResellCo (will appear on the AWS invoice).
- AWS marketplace fee: standard listing fee (~12%) as noted by AWS — this will be visible on the invoice; Redwood is not absorbing the AWS fee.
- Customer discounting: apply a committed-volume discount of 12% off Redwood list price for year 1; tiered renewals to be discussed.
- Expected net to Redwood after fees and infra: ~30% gross margin per Finance modeling.

Attachments: reseller-agreement-draft.pdf (draft reseller SOW and responsibilities), pricing-workbook-v3.xlsx (finalized scenario), DocuSign link for quick signature: https://www.docusign.net/contract/EXAMPLE-DS-12345

Next steps:
1) Taylor (ResellCo) — confirm acceptance of 12% revshare and provide reseller billing/legal contact so AWS can register the partner.
2) Alex / Acme — confirm approval of the proposed discount and that procurement is ok with the marketplace invoice structure.
3) Rohit (AWS) — if you can validate the invoice breakout in your sandbox and confirm the partner registration steps, we can generate the Private Offer and push to DocuSign.

If all good, I'll circulate the final private offer and reseller SOW for signatures this week.

Thanks — Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: reseller-agreement-draft.pdf, pricing-workbook-v3.xlsx, DocuSign link
